museumPlaque.caption: The watch that introduced me to the world of automatic movements.

story.opening: Every collector remembers their first automatic watch. This one will always be mine.
story.background: When I decided it was finally time to buy my first automatic watch, I spent weeks researching the options. I compared watches from Alba, Invicta and several smaller brands, trying to find the best balance between quality, design and value.
story.acquisition: Although there were less expensive choices available, I kept coming back to the Timex Marlin. Eventually, I decided to stretch my budget rather than settle for something I wasn't completely convinced about. Looking back, it was the right decision.
story.experience: The deep blue dial, vintage-inspired design and smooth automatic movement immediately made the watch feel special. I later replaced the original black leather strap with a Jubilee bracelet, giving it a completely different personality while retaining everything I loved about the watch itself. More importantly, it became the first automatic movement I owned and the watch that deepened my appreciation for traditional mechanical watchmaking.
story.whyItMatters: This watch marks one of the biggest milestones in my collecting journey—the transition from quartz watches to automatic movements.
story.favoriteMemory: Putting on my first automatic watch and feeling the smooth sweep of the seconds hand, knowing I had finally reached a milestone I had been looking forward to for years.
story.reflection: Every collection has defining moments. Buying my first automatic was one of them. It wasn't simply another watch; it represented a new chapter in how I appreciated horology.
story.collectorReflection: The first automatic watch doesn't just change your collection. It changes the way you look at every watch that follows.

analytics.lifeLesson: Some Milestones Are Worth Waiting For

book.chapterQuote: The first automatic watch doesn't just tell time—it marks a new chapter in a collector's journey.
